_: Kill-check for the one resolution chain `asc-xagi` gives a single identity. The defect it closes (`dogfood/0082`) was two implementations of one invariant disagreeing -- the generated shell decides which `asc` a hook runs, and `resolveHookBinary` decides which one `asc doctor` reports -- so the mutants below are mostly DIVERGENCE mutants: they break one implementation and leave the other, which is the failure a fix that hand-edited only the shell would have shipped. M1 is exactly that mutant, and it is the reason the branch is rendered from HOOK_BINARY_ORDER rather than written twice. The killers were found empirically rather than guessed: each mutant was applied, install-hook.test.ts and doctor.test.ts were run with vitest's JSON reporter, and the failing test names were read off its assertionResults. There is NO intended survivor, and that is the honest result rather than an omission: every mutant here is observable, so declaring one equivalent would have meant inventing one.
